title: Function norm of a finite locally free morphism of positive constant degree
statement:
Let $f:Y	o X$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes of constant degree $d\geq1$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For every open $V\subseteq X$ there are maps $
u_V:\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ preserving multiplication and $1$ and commuting with restriction to open subsets. They satisfy $
u_V(f^\sharp a)=a^d$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$. For every $b\in\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $y\in f^{-1}V$, $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(f(y))=0$, where the values are in residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. The maps can be chosen with the following local determinant characterization: on every affine open $U\subseteq V$ on which $f_*\mathcal O_Y$ is free of rank $d$, the restriction of $
u_V(b)$ is the determinant of the $d	imes d$ matrix of multiplication by $b|_{f^{-1}U}$ in any basis. Here $\det(A)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^d A_{i,\sigma(i)}$. No reducedness, separability or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=f_*\mathcal O_Y$. By [lem-pc-flf-properties] it is locally free of rank $d$. Thus [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] supplies open trivializations $\mathcal E|_T\simeq\mathcal O_T^{\oplus d}$. Refine them inside the requested open $V$ by affine opens $U$: affine neighbourhoods form a basis by the definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On each such $U$, taking sections of the trivialization gives $D_U=\Gamma(f^{-1}U,\mathcal O_Y)\simeq R_U^d$, where $R_U=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$. Moreover $f^{-1}U$ is affine, since $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The trivialization restricts to every open subset of $U$; in particular every smaller affine open still has a $d$-element basis. No finiteness of the chosen open cover or affineness of its pairwise intersections is assumed.

For any affine $U$ on which $\mathcal E$ is free of rank $d$, apply [lem-a1-principal-free-algebra-determinant-norm] to $R_U\to D_U$, with $r=d$ and the singleton principal cover given by $1\in R_U$. Its hypotheses hold because $D_U$ already has a $d$-element basis. Denote its norm by $N_U$. The same node, with the ring map $R_U\to R_U$ and that basis, gives $N_U(b)=\det(m_b)$ in every basis. Its final affine-open clause applies because $f_*\mathcal O_Y$ is locally free, hence quasi-coherent by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Consequently for every affine $W\subseteq U$ the restriction of $N_U(b)$ equals the determinant of multiplication by $b|_{f^{-1}W}$ in the restricted basis. Changing this basis leaves that determinant unchanged by [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant].

Fix $b\in\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$. On each chart $U$ of step 1 take $N_U(b|_{f^{-1}U})$. To compare charts $U,U'$, cover $U\cap U'$ by affine opens $W$ contained in the intersection. Step 2 identifies both restricted sections on $W$ with the determinant of the same multiplication endomorphism; basis independence [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] makes them equal. The equality and gluing axioms of the structure sheaf [def-pc-scheme] now give a unique section $\nu_V(b)$ with these restrictions. This is an application of the sheaf axiom to the compatible family just constructed. It is independent of the chart cover: compare the two families on affine refinements of their intersections and use uniqueness. Adding any specified free affine $U\subseteq V$ to the cover gives the asserted determinant characterization on that $U$, in any basis. For $V=\varnothing$ the empty family glues to the unique section.

For an open inclusion $V'\subseteq V$, cover $V'$ by free affine charts $U\subseteq V'$. The characterization in step 3 says both $
u_V(b)|_U$ and $
u_{V'}(b|_{f^{-1}V'})|_U$ equal $\det(m_{b|_{f^{-1}U}})$. The equality axiom [def-pc-scheme] therefore proves $
u_V(b)|_{V'}=
u_{V'}(b|_{f^{-1}V'})$. This also proves the compatibility when either open is empty. Thus these sectionwise functions constitute a restriction-compatible map of multiplicative sheaves once the multiplication identity below is verified.

On a free affine chart, $m_{bc}=m_b\circ m_c$, so in a common basis $M_{bc}=M_bM_c$. Apply the product identity of [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities], with $n=d\geq1$, to obtain $\det(M_{bc})=\det(M_b)\det(M_c)$. Also $M_1=I_d$. For a pulled-back scalar $f^\sharp a$, multiplication has matrix $(a|_U)I_d$. In the determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], every term except the identity permutation has a zero off-diagonal entry, so these last two determinants are respectively $1$ and $(a|_U)^d$. Equality of sections can be checked on this cover [def-pc-scheme], giving $
u_V(bc)=
u_V(b)
u_V(c)$, $
u_V(1)=1$, and $
u_V(f^\sharp a)=a^d$. These computations hold over any commutative ring, including rings with nilpotents.

Let $y\in f^{-1}V$, put $x=f(y)$, and choose a free affine chart $U\subseteq V$ containing $x$. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $f^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}D$, possible by finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The points $x,y$ correspond to primes $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\mathfrak q\subset D$, with $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The kernel of $D\to\kappa(y)$ is $\mathfrak q$: in $D_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qD_{\mathfrak q}$ an element $c$ vanishes iff some $s\notin\mathfrak q$ has $sc\in\mathfrak q$, iff $c\in\mathfrak q$ by primality [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus $b(y)=0$ means $b|_{f^{-1}U}\in\mathfrak q$. Since $D$ is finite free over $R$, [lem-pd-finite-free-norm-prime-criterion] implies its norm belongs to $\mathfrak p$ (otherwise $b$ avoids every prime over $\mathfrak p$). By step 3 this norm is $\nu_V(b)|_U$, whose value in $\kappa(x)$ is consequently zero by the same residue-field kernel calculation. This proves the required pointwise vanishing without a reducedness, separability or Noetherian assumption.

Step 5: det(AB)=det(A)det(B) with n=d>=1 gives multiplicativity, and the permutation sum gives det(I)=1 and det(aI)=a^d. Step 6: ker(D->kappa(y))=q, and lem-pd-finite-free-norm-prime-criterion (no domain hypothesis) gives N(b) in p. Advisory: the stalk D_q of Spec is used without its own citation; it is part of the definition of Spec. Tested on X empty, d=1, R^d, k[eps]/eps^2 and the zero ring. lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteLocallyFree_functionNorm {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) [f.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d] : ∃ ν : ∀ V : X.Opens, Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ V) →* Γ(X, V), (∀ (V W : X.Opens) (hWV : W ≤ V) (b : Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ V)), X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWV).op (ν V b) = ν W (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (f.preimage_mono hWV)).op b)) ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), ν V (f.app V a) = a ^ d) ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (b : Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ V)) (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), Y.evaluation (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) y hy b = 0 → X.evaluation V (f y) hy (ν V b) = 0) ∧ (∀ (V U : X.Opens) (hUV : U ≤ V), IsAffineOpen U → ∀ (e : @Module.Basis (Fin d) Γ(X, U) Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) inferInstance inferInstance (f.app U).hom.toModule) (b : Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ V)), X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hUV).op (ν V b) = Matrix.det (f.sectionMultiplicationMatrix U d e (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (f.preimage_mono hUV)).op b)))
lean.note: The fully defined sectionMultiplicationMatrix uses the canonical module structure induced by f.app U; its i,j entry is the i-coordinate of b times the jth basis vector. The theorem supplies the single global restriction-compatible family, with all four clauses of the node. No statement correction.
